lead: Personal computers and everything plugged into or built into them, from laptops and PC parts to enthusiast keyboards, vintage machines and maker boards, organised by function and, for hobbyist areas, by line, generation and archetype.

depts.note: Tier for everyday laptops and desktops; variety for enthusiast lines and vintage machines.

b.v: RTINGS, Notebookcheck, Which?, Consumer Reports, CHOICE scores
b.w: Mainstream buyers pick from tested machines.

b.v: processor tier; GPU tier; RAM; storage
b.w: Sets what the machine can do and for how long.

b.v: chassis material; panel type and resolution; tested battery life
b.w: What separates good machines in daily use.

b.v: iFixit score; upgradeable RAM/SSD; years of updates

s.brief: Organise by line → generation, not SKU. Archetypes = model lines that persist across generations, ordered by significance: Apple PowerBook/MacBook Air/MacBook Pro, IBM/Lenovo ThinkPad (T, X, X1 Carbon), Dell XPS, HP Spectre/EliteBook, Microsoft Surface Laptop, Razer Blade, ASUS ROG Zephyrus, Framework Laptop, Toshiba/Dynabook; historic icons (Toshiba T1100, Compaq LTE, IBM ThinkPad 700C, Apple PowerBook 100). Versions = generations with years. Cut the 3,681-model list (AST, Bondwell etc.) to these lines plus market-covering brands; old vintage laptops may become versions of historic archetypes. Gaming, business, rugged, convertible = types.

k.brief: Types: ultrabook, gaming, workstation, business, rugged, convertible (360° hinge).
Surface Pro line → generation as the archetype.
Pixelbook and market-covering Chromebook lines; keep short.

s.brief: Tier shelf with enthusiast icons. Archetypes: Apple iMac (G3 to Apple silicon), Mac mini, Mac Studio, Mac Pro (cheese grater, trash can), Intel NUC, Dell OptiPlex, HP Z workstations, Alienware Aurora (single-board computers live under Electronics). Trim tower/desktop lists to market brands; vintage desktop-case machines (DEC, Commodore, Atari) move to the Vintage shelf as versions there. Rack-mount servers: keep only homelab-relevant lines (Dell PowerEdge, HPE ProLiant MicroServer), no SKU lists.

k.brief: Types: prebuilt gaming, workstation, office.
Rename from low-profile desktop; types: SFF, USFF, desktop case.
Rack-mount and tower servers owned for homelab use; kind-level, few lines.

s.brief: Variety shelf, collector view. Archetypes with originator, year and versions: Apple I, Apple II (II, II+, IIe, IIc, IIgs), compact Macintosh (128K, 512K, Plus, SE, SE/30, Classic), Commodore PET, VIC-20, Commodore 64 (C64, C64C, SX-64), Amiga (1000, 500, 2000, 1200, 4000), Sinclair ZX80/ZX81/ZX Spectrum (16K/48K, +, 128, +2, +3), BBC Micro (Model A/B, Master), Acorn Electron/Archimedes, Atari 400/800/XL/XE, Atari ST, TRS-80, IBM PC 5150/XT/AT, Amstrad CPC/PCW, MSX, NEC PC-88/PC-98, NeXTcube; portables Osborne 1, Compaq Portable, TRS-80 Model 100. Re-creations (The C64, ZX Spectrum Next, Mega65) as their own kind. Pocket computers: Sharp PC-1211/PC-1500, TRS-80 PC. Trainer kits: KIM-1, Heathkit, Micro-Professor. Floppy drive: Commodore 1541, Apple Disk II, Gotek emulators.

k.brief: 8/16-bit machines with the computer in the keyboard case.
Separate-case micros and early PCs: Apple II, compact Mac, IBM PC, Amiga 2000, NeXT.
Osborne 1, Compaq Portable, Kaypro, TRS-80 Model 100, early PowerBooks.
Modern licensed or FPGA re-creations: The C64/The A500 Mini, ZX Spectrum Next, Mega65.
Vintage and USB floppy drives, Gotek floppy emulators.

depts.note: Parts department: builders compare and upgrade; variety for CPU and GPU lines, tier for the rest.

b.v: Tom's Hardware, TechPowerUp, Gamers Nexus, AnandTech results
b.w: Builders choose parts on measured performance.

80 PLUS / Cybenetics rating; dBA under load

s.brief: Processor: line → generation → SKU. Archetypes: Intel Core (i3/i5/i7/i9, Core Ultra) with generations (Sandy Bridge … Raptor Lake, Arrow Lake), AMD Ryzen (Zen 1–5, X3D), Ryzen Threadripper, Apple M-series (stub; not sold separately — note), Intel Xeon stub, historic icons (Intel 4004, 8086, 80386, Pentium, Athlon, Athlon 64, Core 2 Duo). Versions = generations with years and key SKUs only; cut the 2,857-SKU list. Motherboard: chipset/form-factor types, maker lines (ASUS ROG/TUF/ProArt, MSI MEG/MPG, Gigabyte AORUS, ASRock Taichi). Merge board-with-CPU into Motherboard. Memory: merge desktop and laptop RAM; types DDR3/DDR4/DDR5, DIMM/SODIMM; lines Corsair Vengeance/Dominator, G.Skill Trident Z, Kingston Fury, Crucial.

k.brief: Type 'with CPU fitted' replaces the separate kind.
Types: desktop DIMM, laptop SODIMM; DDR generation.

s.brief: Graphics card: consumer lines → generation, by significance: Nvidia GeForce (256, 8800, GTX 10, RTX 20/30/40/50), AMD/ATI Radeon (9700, HD, RX 400–9000), Intel Arc, 3dfx Voodoo (Voodoo, Voodoo2, Voodoo5); board partners (ASUS ROG Strix, MSI Gaming X, Sapphire Nitro+, EVGA) as versions/brands, not SKU lists; drop workstation/datacentre SKUs. Sound card: Creative Sound Blaster (16, AWE32, Live!, Audigy), Roland MT-32/LAPC-I for retro collectors. Merge internal and external capture devices into one kind (Elgato HD60/4K lines).

k.brief: Types: internal, USB; retro collector cards.
Types: internal card, external USB.
